title: Revisiting the Generic Transformer: Deconstructing a Strong Baseline for Time Series Foundation Models
claim: A plain encoder-only patch Transformer with masking, normalization and quantile outputs is a simple, complete forecasting recipe.
layout: Single vertical column, bottom-to-top flow, dashed skip arrow for mean/std

The band holds a blue time-series line plot with two translucent blue regions labeled 'Contiguous Patch Masking'. Above it come the boxes 'Mask-aware Normalization' (light blue), 'Patch Embedding (Residual Block)' (purple), 'Full-Attention Transformer Blocks' (red, the focal block), 'Quantile Head (Residual Block)' (purple) and 'Reverse Normalization' (light blue). abstract: The recent surge of interest in Time Series Foundation Models has rapidly advanced the field. Yet, heterogeneous training setups across studies make it difficult to determine whether performance improvements came from architectural innovations or effective data engineering. In this work, we investigate whether a standard patch Transformer architecture, paired with a straightforward training protocol, can match the zero-shot forecasting performance of state-of-the-art TSFMs. We conduct a comprehensive ablation study covering model scaling, data composition, and training techniques to examine the ingredients behind this performance. Our findings show that pretraining data composition, contiguous patch masking, and context length have a substantial effect on forecasting accuracy, and that the generic architecture itself can deliver high performance with good scalability. By strictly controlling these experimental variables, we provide comprehensive empirical results on model scaling across multiple dimensions. Furthermore, we establish that the effectiveness of this training protocol generalizes robustly across benchmarks and alternative architectures. We release our pretrained models and document the detailed training protocol and findings to establish a transparent, reproducible baseline for future research.
